cards.explanation: The answer is the Spirit. Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes that these exiles were "…sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ…" (1 Peter 1:2). Look at who shows up in that one verse, friends: God the Father, the Spirit and Jesus Christ. Peter puts all three right there in his greeting.

The answer is a living hope. Peter says God "…has given us new birth into a living hope…" (1 Peter 1:3). Not a dead hope, not a maybe-someday hope, a LIVING one, friends. And he says it comes by God's great mercy, so nobody has to earn it with a perfect batch.

The answer is the resurrection. Peter says the living hope comes "…through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead…" (1 Peter 1:3). The hope is alive because Jesus is risen, friends. That's the whole reason the oven stays on in my bakery.

The answer is False. Peter says the inheritance is "…imperishable, undefiled, and unfading…" (1 Peter 1:4). It doesn't spoil, it doesn't get stained, and it doesn't fade. And it's reserved in heaven for them, so it's already put away safe.

The word is power. Peter says these believers "…are shielded by God’s power…" (1 Peter 1:5). Shielded, friends. That's not me holding the oven door shut with my mustache, that's God's own power doing the guarding.

The answer is True. Peter says gold "…perishes even though refined by fire…" (1 Peter 1:7). Gold goes through the fire and still perishes. And he says the proven character of their faith is more precious than that. I'd take that trade any day of the week.

The answer is at the revelation of Jesus Christ. Peter says their proven faith "…may result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ." (1 Peter 1:7). He points to that moment, not to some earlier finish line, friends. And he never says when that is, so I keep my ovens ready.

The answer is True. Peter writes, "Though you have not seen Him, you love Him…" (1 Peter 1:8). They've never laid eyes on Jesus, and they love Him anyway. They also believe in Him and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy.

The answer is salvation. Peter says they are "…receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls." (1 Peter 1:9). That's the goal, friends, the finished box. And he says they're receiving it now.

The answer is His sufferings and the glories to follow. Peter says the Spirit of Christ in the prophets "…predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories to follow." (1 Peter 1:11). Sufferings first, glories after. I think that order is worth slowing down for.

The answer is Peter's readers. Peter says it was revealed to the prophets "…that they were not serving themselves, but you…" (1 Peter 1:12). The "you" is the folks reading his letter. Those prophets searched and investigated carefully, and they were serving Peter's readers all along. I feel that in my mustache.

The answer is True. The last line of the passage says, "Even angels long to look into these things." (1 Peter 1:12). Angels, friends. Peter says they long to look into the very things the gospel preachers announced. I think that makes the good news pretty special.
